questions.q_en: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in present indefinite tense.

options_en: He sends messages to his friends every day.

He will send messages to his friends every day.
He used to send messages to his friends every day.
options_hi: He sends messages to his friends every day.

He will send messages to his friends every day.
He used to send messages to his friends every day.
questions.solution_en:
The correct option that expresses the given sentence in the present indefinite tense is (a).

The present indefinite tense, also known as the present simple tense, is used to describe actions that are habitual, routine, or generally true. It is formed by using the base form of the verb for most subjects, with the third person singular (he, she, it) adding an -s to the verb.

Subject: "He" (pronoun indicating the person who performs the action)

Verb: "sends" (base form of the verb with the added -s for the third person singular)

Object: "messages to his friends every day" (what is being sent and how often)

b) - simple past tense [sent]

c) - simple future tense [will send]

d) - simple past tense [used to send]

questions.q_en:
Select the appropriate option for the given blank-

He is standing at the edge of the dance floor and is not ________.
questions.q_hi:
Select the appropriate option for the given blank-

He is standing at the edge of the dance floor and is not ________.
questions.solution_en:
As per the syntax of present continuous tense- Subject+ is/am/are + not + verb +ing.

We have to follow the rule of parallelism here as the two actions 'standing on the edge' and 'not dancing' are joined by the conjunction 'and'.

The use of 'dancing' is appropriate.

The correct sentence is- He is standing at the edge of the dance floor and is not dancing.

Hence, option (d) is correct.

Note: Parallelism: In grammar, parallelism, also known as parallel structure or parallel construction, is a balance within one or more sentences of similar phrases or clauses that have the same grammatical structure. Given below is an example which shows a sentence in two forms (parallel in structure and lacking parallelism): Lacking parallelism: Prerna likes cooking, dancing and to sing. Parallel: Prerna likes cooking, dancing and singing.
